main_text.p: epilepsia, caro. Balani autem acres ex melle, & sale, acriores mistis purgantibus prædictis fient.
Cucurbitulæ etiam inter scapulio & cerui cibus affixæ, in id salutares sunt: nec inutilia sunt repellentia, vt lib.13. meth. in lethargo.

Pituitam à capite reliquam dissipantibus, vel sumptis (vt diamosci dulcis, vel amari Mesuæ, vel pliris arcotic. Nicolai drachmis duabus, vel theriaces aut mithridatij veteris drachma vna semel in hebdomade sumpta mane, horis septem ante cibum: vel acoro codito, vel confectione ex acoro tota sua sub statia in id efficaci, horis duabus ante cibum per se, aut cum aqua maiorana, bethonica, saluia, vel alterius capitalis facultate simi-lis) vel admotis vnctionibus, irrigationibus, fotibus, cataplasmatis, emplastris, sacculis, odoramentis, ac reliquis topicis remedijs, ex oleo anethino chamæmeli, liliorum, costino, balanino, ex decocto capitalium prædictorum in lixiuio, euphorbio, castoreo, quæ etiam in aurem tuto à Galeno immittuntur, ne capiti cum
Auicen. cociliator Acorus sit indicus non no-stras.

page.notes: Marginal note left, beside the lines "Pituitam" to "ris drachma": "Auicen. cociliator Acorus sit indicus non nostras." Printed as a note; the first line of the note block is shown as foot text. Catchword "cum" at the right foot is taken as the last line of text, not a catchword. Some letters in the Greek-less passage are uncertain, including "scapulio" and "Mesuæ".
